title: TRIBE
subtitle: Designing an early-stage platform to test interest in a new community.
content:
TRIBE was an idea that needed to be tested, not just designed.

I worked with Native Earth to turn an early-stage concept into a tangible product experience ahead of the 2025 NDIS Expo in Perth.

The first challenge was understanding the platform's two-sided audience: Participants and Providers. Through competitor analysis and product exploration, I identified how each audience would interact with TRIBE and where the experience needed to create value for both sides.

With only three weeks to bring the concept to life, I focused on the core experiences that could communicate the product quickly and clearly. Rather than designing the entire platform, I created a focused set of app experiences that demonstrated discovery, connections and community events.

The expo then became an opportunity to test the proposition in the real world. I designed the physical experience around a simple journey: see, understand, scan, sign up. QR codes connected the expo banners directly to the digital experience, allowing visitors to move from curiosity to engagement with minimal friction.

The result was more than a polished concept. TRIBE had something tangible to put in front of its audience and use to gauge interest in the platform.

The project reinforced an important product principle for me: when you're working with an unvalidated idea, the goal isn't to design everything. It's to design enough to learn.
